newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish GDP rises 7.8 pct, GNP up 6.9 pct in 1996 - CSO.
newsitem.headline: Irish GDP rises 7.8 pct, GNP up 6.9 pct in 1996 - CSO.

text.p: Irish gross domestic product (GDP) rose by 7.8 percent in 1996 while gross national product (GNP) growth was 6.9 percent last year, the Central Statistics Office (CSO) said on Thursday.
Analysts' GDP forecasts had ranged from 5.8 to 7.9 percent while they predicted GNP growth would be between 4.8 and 8.0 percent.
Buoyant consumer spending, which rose by 6.3 percent in volume terms over 1995, contributed to the rise in the 1996 aggregates, the CSO said.
It said there was also a sizeable increase in investment in capital goods which rose 15.9 percent in volume terms.
The figures showed a slowdown in the volume of exports of goods and services to 10 percent from an average of 16.9 percent in the previous two years.
Imports growth also slowed to 11.4 percent in 1996 compared with an average of 15.3 percent for the previous two years, the CSO said.

"The gap between exports and imports at constant 1990 prices continued to widen by 215 million punts in 1996 but at a slower rate than in the previous two years when it increased on average by 980 million punts," the research and statistics body said.
It said the biggest impact on the trade balance was a sharp increase in service imports, including royalties.
Service imports in 1996 exceeded those of 1995 by 1.154 billion or 19 percent, it said.

In current money values, personal expenditure rose by 7.5 percent and government expenditure by 5.0 percent, giving real increases of 6.3 percent and 2.9 percent respectively, when prise rises are discounted, the CSO said.

It said the value of investment in new buildings and capital equipment rose by 18.5 percent in money values which is equivalent to 15.9 percent in real terms. The value of stocks rose by 389 million Irish pounds during 1996, it said.
